messages:
morgan: Heads-up — I opened a PR that flattens the payments module and adjusts provider pins. Can someone do a quick compat check? I want to avoid a lockfile/regression surprise in staging. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/4822 :wave:

elaine: looking now. quick q — are we moving to the single root provider only (hoisted) or keeping module-level pins for EKS modules?

morgan: hoisting to root provider s.t. we can manage provider versions centrally, but leaving an explicit required_providers block in the module to keep terraform cloud happy. main goal is fewer duplicated entries in the lockfile and easier upgrades.

javier: FYI the k8s secret path for payments changed last month (secrets/payment -> secrets/services/payments). If TF state referencers aren't updated we'll break application sync. Did the PR include a state migration mapping?

morgan: good catch — I added a small state mv in the plan stage but not a full backfill. I planned to run a canary in staging first. snippet I used: 
```
terraform state mv module.payments.kubernetes_secret.payment module.payments.kubernetes_secret.payment_new_path
```
but that was local. Open to a safer approach.

sam: +1 to canary. For provider lockfile: run `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=linux_arm64` after pinning. Otherwise CI will show mismatched providers on plan.

ci-bot: plan failed on branch flatten-payments: provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/kubernetes: version constraint mismatch (expected 2.11.0, got 2.8.1). See full plan output: https://ci.internal/builds/7123

elaine: ok that explains the failure. If we want to move to 2.11.0 we should:
- update required_providers in root 
- regen lockfile (as Sam said)
- run `terraform init -upgrade` in staging workspace

javier: about the secret path, can we add a small wrapper that keeps both paths available for reads during rollout? i.e. read old path first fallback to new path, then later switch to only new. That minimizes downtime.

morgan: yep plan is to add compatibility accessor in the Helm values and a short-lived migration job. Example values change I pushed to the helm chart: 
```yaml
secrets:
  paymentPath: "/secrets/services/payments"
  legacyPaths:
    - "/secrets/payment"
```

sam: also add a terraform lint check that fails when any module still has `provider =` blocks pointing to module-level providers — we want to avoid accidental reintroductions. I can draft a tflint rule.

elaine: for the lockfile regen, small checklist: 
1) bump root required_providers version constraint
2) run `terraform init -upgrade` locally
3) run `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=linux_arm64` and commit `.terraform.lock.hcl`
4) run plan in staging Workspace (with state mv applied as a separate transaction)

morgan: thanks — I'll follow that. Quick ask: who can give the actual staging plan LGTM once CI passes? @elaine? :eyes:

elaine: happy to once CI green and secret path migration job is scheduled.

infra-bot: reminder — schedule a maintenance window for state moves touching >10 resources. Add `#infra-maintenance` to the PR description and ping eng-oncall.

morgan: noted, will update PR desc.

ci-bot: re-run requested. Plan started for flatten-payments (build 7126) — we'll post results here when ready.

sam: minimal sed to update k8s secret references in TF manifests if needed: 
```bash
grep -R "secrets/payment" -n | xargs sed -i 's|/secrets/payment|/secrets/services/payments|g'
```
use with caution and review diffs.

javier: I'll validate the helm canary job and the migration pod. If we see any mismatches on the canary, we'll abort and revert.

morgan: thanks all — will update PR with lockfile + maintenance window + migration job. tagging for follow-ups: @sam for tflint rule, @javier for helm canary, @elaine for staging LGTM. :thumbsup:
